classes.name: Testosterone replacement
classes.description: Testosterone gel/solution (AndroGel, Testim, Fortesta, Vogelxo, generic 1%/1.62%), injections (cypionate, enanthate, Xyosted, Aveed undecanoate), patch (Androderm), oral undecanoate (Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex), nasal (Natesto), pellets (Testopel).
classes.plainDescription: Testosterone replacement for low testosterone, as a gel, shot or pill.

preferredAgent.strength: 200 mg/mL (standard label strength; not printed in MHDL)
preferredAgent.sig: 50-400 mg IM every 2 to 4 weeks, adjusted to keep morning testosterone in the normal range (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: A shot every 2 to 4 weeks; your prescriber sets the dose from blood tests.

records.preferredRestriction: PA required: appropriate diagnosis and two low total testosterone results (under 300 ng/dL) drawn within 3 months of each other, per MHDL androgen criteria

paRequired.reason: PA at any age; Xyosted also needs a trial of testosterone cypionate and enanthate injection (or needle phobia plus two topical trials)
criteria: Adult hypogonadism: two total testosterone levels under 300 ng/dL (3 months apart at most, within a year of the request); Xyosted also: failed cypionate and enanthate (90 days), or needle phobia plus two failed topicals.
Delayed puberty or pediatric hypogonadism: pediatric endocrinologist prescribing, Tanner stage I-II or other delayed-puberty signs, and one total testosterone below 300 ng/dL within a year.
Gender dysphoria, transgenderism, or therapy after gender reassignment surgery: diagnosis documented; testosterone levels not required.

records.stepTherapy: Several androgen products require a trial or contraindication to testosterone cypionate injection and/or enanthate injection (MHDL Androgens criteria). Two dated lab tests (within 3 months, drawn within 1 year, total testosterone under 300 ng/dL) are required for the Azmiro criteria.
records.verificationNote: Testosterone cypionate chosen as preferred agent because other androgen criteria reference it as the baseline product. The cypionate-specific criteria paragraph was only partly read; the lab criteria shown are from the Azmiro paragraph and the general androgen language. Pediatric paragraphs (delayed puberty, hypogonadism under 18) exist but do not apply to adult preferred pick. Aveed carries the MB flag, so it may fall under the medical benefit. [Sonnet check 2026-10-22: Table 55 (id 91) criteria re-read: testosterone cypionate needs appropriate diagnosis and two total-testosterone results under 300 ng/dL dated at most 3 months apart and drawn within a year; SmartPA may auto-process with a history of hypogonadism claims. Depo-Testosterone and generic share one PA row. Pediatric hypogonadism and gender dysphoria have separate criteria. Chosen over oral methyltestosterone (plain PA, needs failed Jatenzo/Tlando plus two non-injectable trials). Upgraded to verified.] [2026-10-22 review: sig replaced with label dosing by indication/titration.]

records.verificationNote: Read p. 28. Methyltestosterone capsules (and Methitest tablets) are the only no-PA androgens on the list, so the preferred pick follows the no-PA rule. Judgment call: injectable testosterone is the more common first-line therapy and it carries PA here. Xyosted, Aveed, Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex, Androderm, Testopel and Azmiro are not printed; list is not complete, so unconfirmed. Injectable forms may be provider-administered and billed under the medical benefit, which the list does not state. [Sonnet check 2026-10-22: re-read p. 28. Pick changed from oral methyltestosterone (no PA but not a standard TRT product) to testosterone cypionate injection, the standard first-line product, with its PA in preferredRestriction. Methyltestosterone and Methitest moved to alternatives. Gel row 'Except authorized generics for TESTIM and VOGELXO' is unexplained, so partial. Cypionate may be self-injected or clinic-given; the list does not say.] [2026-10-22 review: sig replaced with label dosing by indication/titration.]
